module8: Capstone: set up and audit a whole company suite
Bring every module together. You build a small working company in the suite, then check it like an outside reviewer.
Plan one end-to-end story: lead, deal, invoice, payment, support ticket.
Check that each app passes data to the next one without retyping.
Audit roles, automations and logs for gaps and risks.
Teach a colleague to use the suite in 20 minutes.
A reviewer follows one customer from web form to paid invoice and finds that the ticket app does not know the invoice is paid. You add a rule to fix it.
Build the full story with three users, run five customers through it, then write a one-page audit with three problems and fixes.
Every customer completes the story; audit lists three problems with a fix and an owner for each.
quiz: A new employee needs to see deals but not the bank feed. Which part of the suite do you change?
You set a role for that user so it only allows the sales app and hides the books app. Roles control who sees which data, so you do not share one login.
A web form on your site should create a lead and give a task to a salesperson. What two things do you set up?
You build the form with the fields you need and link it to the lead list, then add a rule that creates a task and assigns it to a named person when a lead arrives.
A customer invoice is 7 days overdue. How can the suite handle this without manual work?
Set an automatic reminder rule that sends a polite email at 7 days overdue. Check the aged receivables report to see which invoices are still open.
Explain why the three books reports (profit and loss, balance sheet, aged receivables) are used together.
Profit and loss shows if you earned money in a period, the balance sheet shows what you own and owe on one date, and aged receivables shows who has not paid yet. Together they give the full picture.
Ten tickets arrive and four are the same question about delivery times. What is the best fix?
Write one knowledge article that answers it and link it in the reply template. Then agents stop answering the same question again and again.
A ticket has a service level of 4 hours and it is now hour 5 with no reply. What does this mean and what do you do?
The service level is missed. Raise the ticket priority, assign an owner now, and check why it waited so you can change the rule or staffing.
A project reaches a milestone and you want an invoice created. How does linking help?
If the milestone is linked to billing, completing it creates an invoice draft automatically. This saves time and stops you forgetting to bill.
You build a rule: when a new customer is added in the sales app, create a contact in the books app. What must you do before turning it on?
Test it with a practice record in test mode, check the log for errors, and set an error message so someone is told if it fails.
Compare rolling out the suite to everyone on one day with a pilot team first.
A pilot with a small team for two weeks finds problems early and keeps the risk low. A one-day rollout is faster but mistakes hit the whole company at once.
In the capstone audit you find that an automation silently fails when a customer has no email. What do you recommend?
Add a check for the empty field, create a fault path that notifies a named person, and write the fix and its owner in the audit. Then test again with an empty-email record.
ladder: L1 Basic: Know the suite
Remember the names of the main apps and what each one is for. You can open the launcher and sign in with one login.
Show the launcher on screen and ask learners to name each app out loud. Common mistake: thinking each app needs its own account.
L2 Awareness: See how data flows
Understand how a lead becomes a deal, an invoice and a payment. You can explain in your own words why shared data saves time.
Draw the customer story on a board and let learners point to each hand-off. Check they can say why retyping causes errors.
L3 Foundation: Do simple tasks
Apply the basics: add a user, capture a lead, raise an invoice and log an expense. You follow a checklist to finish each task correctly.
Give a short checklist and watch a learner do each task once. Common mistake: giving a user too many rights because it is quicker.
L4 Practitioner: Run daily work
Analyse your own books, tickets and pipeline to find what is late or wrong. You read the reports and decide what to fix first.
Hand out a practice month with three hidden errors and ask learners to find them. Check that they match reports to the bank.
L5 Specialist: Build rules and automations
Evaluate which routine jobs are worth automating and build tested rules for them. You check logs and set error paths before going live.
Ask learners to justify each automation by time saved and risk. Common mistake: switching a rule on without a test record.
L6 Advanced: Design for a company
Create a rollout plan with waves, training, data protection settings and a dashboard. You set rules that fit how the company really works.
Review each plan for a pilot, a backup and an export. Check the plan names an owner for every step.
L7 Super expert: Audit and teach
Evaluate a whole suite like an outside reviewer and create a plan to fix it. You can train others and improve the setup year after year.
Let the learner audit a messy sample company and teach back in 20 minutes. Look for clear risks, simple fixes and plain language.
